vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: skillup
Version: 0.1.7

SkillUp is a legitimate automation utility designed to package and publish OpenClaw skills to multiple platforms including GitHub, Xiaping, and ClawHub. The bundle contains a comprehensive suite of shell scripts (scripts/publish.sh and its libraries) that handle API tokens and perform network uploads via curl and platform-specific CLIs (gh, claw, clawhub). While the tool manages sensitive credentials, its behavior is strictly aligned with its stated purpose, and the code follows defensive programming practices (e.g., using CDPATH= cd and localized Python helpers for safe parsing). No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, or prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (packaging and publishing skills) matches the files, binaries, and environment variables it asks for; nothing in the scripts suggests behavior outside that scope.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included shell scripts: the code implements packaging and multi-platform publishing to GitHub, Xiaping, OpenClaw, and ClawHub. The required binaries (curl, git, gh, claw, clawhub, zip/python3) and the tokens requested are exactly what a multi-platform publisher would need.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the publish.sh entrypoint with typical parameters. The scripts operate on skill directories, manifest/SKILL.md frontmatter, produce zip artifacts, call platform APIs/CLIs, and write results to an artifact/result file. They read config files and environment variables that are declared. There are no instructions to read unrelated system files, user shell history, SSH keys, or other secrets outside the declared env vars and configurable paths.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with shell scripts included; there is no remote download/install step. All code is local shell/python scripts (no external arbitrary URL downloads or extraction), so install risk is low.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested environment variables correspond to the four target platforms (SKILLUP_GITHUB_TOKEN, SKILLUP_XIAPING_API_KEY, SKILLUP_OPENCLAW_TOKEN, SKILLUP_CLAWHUB_TOKEN) and a CLAWHUB_TOKEN fallback — this is proportional to a tool that can publish to those services. The primary credential is GitHub as declared and used. The scripts do export tokens to CLI environment variables (e.g., GH_TOKEN, CLAWHUB_TOKEN) as expected for CLI-based publishing.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request permanent system-wide privileges. The scripts write artifacts and temporary /tmp logs, modify target repositories only when configured, and do not change other skills' configurations. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but does not combine with other red flags.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for its purpose, but it will execute shell commands that can publish files and call remote APIs. Before installing: (1) prefer running in --dry-run mode first to see what it would do; (2) provide least-privilege tokens (e.g., GitHub PAT scoped only to the target repo or to create releases if needed); (3) inspect and, if desired, pin config.example.toml values (base URLs, upload paths) to known endpoints; (4) ensure the environment has the declared CLIs installed (gh, claw, clawhub) if you want full functionality; and (5) avoid supplying tokens with broad scopes (org/admin access) unless you trust the source. If you have concerns about autonomous execution, do not grant credentials to the runtime or only run publish.sh manually in a controlled environment.
